questions.def: Use the past simple for completed actions in the past.
questions.question: I ___ to the cinema last night.

questions.def: Use past continuous for actions in progress at a specific time.
questions.question: They ___ TV when I arrived.

questions.def: The past simple form of 'eat' is 'ate'.
questions.question: He ___ all his dinner.

questions.def: Use 'have been' for experiences up to now.
questions.question: We ___ to Paris before.

questions.def: Use past simple for a completed action at a stated time.
questions.question: She ___ her keys yesterday.

questions.def: Use past simple, not present continuous, with 'yesterday'.
questions.question: I am seeing him yesterday evening.

questions.def: Use present perfect for actions that started in the past and continue.
questions.question: They ___ here for five years.

questions.def: 'They' is plural, so use 'were' with past continuous.
questions.question: They ___ studying when the phone rang.

questions.def: 'ago' indicates a completed action in the past (past simple).
questions.question: He ___ to the shop an hour ago.

questions.def: Use past simple with 'last week', not present perfect.
questions.question: She has finished her work last week.

questions.def: The past simple of 'make' is 'made'.
questions.question: I ___ a cake yesterday.

questions.def: 'I' is singular, so use 'was' in the past simple.
questions.question: I ___ tired after the long walk.

questions.def: Past simple of 'have' is 'had' for completed actions.
questions.question: We ___ a good time at the beach.

questions.def: Use 'have gone', not 'are gone', to show a completed action.
questions.question: They are gone to the market.

questions.def: The past simple of 'want' is 'wanted'.
questions.question: He ___ to go home earlier.

questions.def: Use 'did not' for negative past simple sentences.
questions.question: She ___ not come to the party.

questions.def: Use past simple for a completed action at a specific time.
questions.question: I ___ the film last night.

questions.def: Use past simple, not present continuous, with 'last summer'.
questions.question: We are visited Italy last summer.

questions.def: Use 'did go' to form past simple questions.
questions.question: Where ___ you ___ last weekend?

questions.def: Use past perfect continuous for actions before another past action.
questions.question: He ___ working here for 10 years before he retired.

questions.def: Use past perfect for actions completed before another past action.
questions.question: By the time I arrived, they ___ all the food.

questions.def: Use past perfect continuous or present perfect continuous with 'since'.
questions.question: She was living in London since 2015.

questions.def: The past simple form of 'work' is 'worked'.
questions.question: I ___ all day yesterday.

questions.def: Use past continuous for ongoing action at a specific time.
questions.question: The sun ___ when I woke up.

questions.def: Past Perfect for actions before another action in the past
questions.question: Before I met him, I ___ never ___ to Spain.

questions.def: Use 'Did see' to form a past simple question.
questions.question: ___ you ___ that movie last week?

questions.def: 'Used to' describes past habits or states.
questions.question: She ___ playing the piano when she was young.

questions.def: Present Perfect Negative to say that an action started in the past.
questions.question: I ___ him since last year.

questions.def: 'Went' is the past simple form of 'go'.
questions.question: Yesterday, I ___ to the store to buy milk.

questions.def: 'Watched' is the correct past simple form.
questions.question: They ___ a movie last night.
